content:
Thanks for your message! You're referring to a known issue in Thunderbird Address Book version 145 (and similar builds), where drag-and-drop into mailing lists (also called distribution lists) no longer works as it did in earlier versions.

✅ The problem: In Thunderbird 115+ (including 145), the address book has been redesigned, and drag & drop behavior is broken or changed:

- You can't drag individual contacts from the main address book into a mailing list anymore. - The mailing list UI doesn't accept dropped items as before.

💡 Workarounds / Solutions: 🛠 1. Manually Add Contacts to the Mailing List

You can still: 1. Open the mailing list by double-clicking it. 2. In the window that opens, type the name or email address of the contact manually. Thunderbird auto-completes based on your address book. 3. Click OK / Save when finished. ⚠ This is tedious for large lists, but still works.

🔄 2. Switch to “Classic” Address Book (if possible) Some users have had success using older Thunderbird versions (e.g. 102.x), where drag & drop still works. - You can install an older portable Thunderbird version alongside the new one for managing contacts.

🧩 3. Use an Add-on (if available) Some Thunderbird extensions (like "Mailing List Tools" or "CardBook") have reintroduced better list handling. Keep an eye on: - https://addons.thunderbird.net - Search for Mailing list management tools or Cardbook 🔍 Compatibility with Thunderbird 145 must be confirmed before use.

⏳ 4. Wait for Fixes This is a known issue, and many users have https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/ and the https://support.mozilla.org/

👉 Developers are likely aware and may fix it in a future update.

🔚 Summary | Option | Status | | ----------------- | ------------------------- | | Drag & Drop | ❌ Currently broken | | Manual entry | ✅ Works, but tedious | | Older Thunderbird | ✅ Drag & drop works there | | Add-ons | 🔄 May help | | Future updates | ⏳ Likely fix coming |

That's one too many. You'll have to find out to which folder messages classified as 'Junk' will be sent to. A pragmatic way to test this is to mark a message as 'Junk', and check where it goes to. You may also check your account via webmail to determine which folder is the one used by your email provider's server. What makes things more difficult is a bug introduced recently, where Thunderbird shows the spam folder used by your email provider's server, e.g. 'Suspected Spam', just as 'Junk'. That bug will be fixed in TB 144 to be released in about two weeks time. So if you're unsure about the correct folder you may just wait until then.
